title: Gaza: food aid cut for half a million people
lines: The UN's World Food Programme has cut food aid to more than half a million people in Gaza, because it is running out of money.
This summer, the WFP was helping feed about one point six million people, around three quarters of Gaza's population.
From October, that has fallen to one point one million people a month.
Food parcels have been halved, from two to one, and daily hot meals have been cut from two hundred and fifty thousand to one hundred and fifty thousand.
The agency says it needs four hundred million euros over the next six months, for Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
About two thirds of Gaza's people face crisis levels of hunger or worse, and around two hundred thousand are one step from famine.
More than two thousand eight hundred children were admitted for malnutrition treatment in September, according to the UN's humanitarian office.
Prices are high. A tray of eggs costs around sixty shekels, nearly twenty dollars, according to Al Jazeera.
Unemployment stands at about eighty percent, according to UN data cited by the Irish Times.
Famine was declared in Gaza City in August last year, and receded after a ceasefire, but the WFP calls those gains very fragile.
Its country director says the situation is still brutal, and that Gaza needs investment in recovery.
